title: A no-model session-load benchmark replays one session's hooks and records each process class's CPU, memory and starts
goal: python3 _tools/benchmarks.py run session-load replays, with no model, the hook events of one Claude Code session through this clone's own hook commands (.claude/settings.json) in a throwaway clone with a scratch query log home (CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA and CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT both set), in arm A (every hook), arm C (coord_hook and the querylog hooks left out) and arm D (no hook), each in phase idle (SessionStart, then SessionEnd) and phase working (with a fixed script of prompt and tool events between), measures every process it starts by os.wait4 rusage and samples, grouped by the host panel's process classes; it writes per phase, arm and class (case '<phase> <class>', 'all' for their sum) the rows cpu_s, rss_peak_mb, rss_mean_mb and spawns_per_min, fewer starts in arm D than C and in C than A; it writes per synchronous hook command a sync_ms row, coord_hook's among them; each cpu_s row's note names host cores, load and warm or cold; and kb/_self/reports/benchmarks.csv holds a 5-rep record of arms A, C and D with its table in kb/_self/reports/benchmarks.md

run:
import sys
def _fail(t, e, tb, _d=sys.excepthook):
    if issubclass(t, AssertionError):
        print('check failed:', e); sys.exit(1)
    _d(t, e, tb)
sys.excepthook = _fail
import csv, os, shutil, subprocess, tempfile
T = tempfile.mkdtemp()
B = os.path.join(T, 'bin'); os.mkdir(B)
open(os.path.join(B, 'claude'), 'w').write('#!/bin/sh\nexit 1\n')
os.chmod(os.path.join(B, 'claude'), 0o755)
ENV = dict(os.environ, PATH=B + os.pathsep + os.environ['PATH'])
out = os.path.join(T, 'out.csv')
p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '_tools/benchmarks.py', 'run', 'session-load', '--arms', 'A,C,D', '--reps', '1', '--out', out],
                   capture_output=True, text=True, env=ENV, timeout=1800)
rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(out, encoding='utf-8'))) if os.path.exists(out) else []
shutil.rmtree(T, ignore_errors=True)
assert p.returncode == 0, ('run session-load exit', p.returncode, p.stderr[-400:])
rows = [r for r in rows if r['scenario'] == 'session-load']
assert not [r for r in rows if r['metric'] in ('errors', 'spend_usd')], 'an errors or spend row: a model ran or a replay failed'
val = {(r['case'], r['arm'], r['metric']): float(r['value']) for r in rows}
for case in ('idle all', 'working all'):
    for arm in 'ACD':
        for m in ('cpu_s', 'rss_peak_mb', 'rss_mean_mb', 'spawns_per_min'):
            assert (case, arm, m) in val, ('no row', case, arm, m)
    assert val[(case, 'D', 'spawns_per_min')] < val[(case, 'C', 'spawns_per_min')] < val[(case, 'A', 'spawns_per_min')], ('spawns not D < C < A', case)
assert [k for k in val if k[1] == 'A' and 'coord_hook' in k[0] and k[2] == 'sync_ms'], 'no sync_ms row for coord_hook in arm A'
assert all('cores' in r['note'] and 'load' in r['note'] and ('warm' in r['note'] or 'cold' in r['note']) for r in rows if r['metric'] == 'cpu_s'), 'a cpu_s row note lacks host cores, load or warm or cold'

gates.question: What divides the starts of a replay into spawns_per_min?
options: the seconds of session a phase stands for, 60 idle and 300 working, the same for every arm
gates.recommendation: the seconds of session a phase stands for, 60 idle and 300 working, the same for every arm
gates.reason: the wall time of an arm with fewer hooks is shorter, so the rate would not fall with the starts
gates.answer: the seconds of session a phase stands for, 60 idle and 300 working, the same for every arm

gates.question: How are the processes a hook command starts counted?
options: an audit hook in a sitecustomize on PYTHONPATH logs each process a Python program starts, so the count is exact for Python and misses a program that is not Python
gates.recommendation: an audit hook in a sitecustomize on PYTHONPATH logs each process a Python program starts, so the count is exact for Python and misses a program that is not Python
gates.reason: the sampler misses processes shorter than a listing, so its count moves with the host's speed
gates.answer: an audit hook in a sitecustomize on PYTHONPATH logs each process a Python program starts, so the count is exact for Python and misses a program that is not Python

gates.question: In what order does a replay run the hook commands of one event?
options: the synchronous ones one after another in file order, the async ones at once and not waited for
every hook of the event at once
gates.recommendation: the synchronous ones one after another in file order, the async ones at once and not waited for
gates.reason: each sync_ms is then the command's own time, not slowed by its siblings
gates.answer: the synchronous ones one after another in file order, the async ones at once and not waited for

gates.question: To which class is the CPU of a hook command's process tree charged?
options: the class of the hook command's own command line, its children's starts and memory counted under their own classes
split among the classes by the share of ps samples
gates.recommendation: the class of the hook command's own command line, its children's starts and memory counted under their own classes
gates.reason: os.wait4 gives the tree's CPU exactly and no per-process CPU of a child that ends within a listing exists to split it by
gates.answer: the class of the hook command's own command line, its children's starts and memory counted under their own classes

gates.question: How does the replay treat the intake hook's drift cursor, which moves a scan to new items each run?
options: remove the cursor before each replay, so every replay scans the same items
leave it, so successive replays scan different items
gates.recommendation: remove the cursor before each replay, so every replay scans the same items
gates.reason: the starts of arm A and C then differ by the hooks left out, not by the items the scan reached
gates.answer: remove the cursor before each replay, so every replay scans the same items

gates.question: How does --arms name the arms of session-load next to the arms of pool?
options: each scenario takes the names it knows (A, C, D for session-load), and pool named with only session-load arms is refused
gates.recommendation: each scenario takes the names it knows (A, C, D for session-load), and pool named with only session-load arms is refused
gates.reason: the goal runs session-load --arms A,C,D, and a refusal keeps pool from running its paid default arms
gates.answer: each scenario takes the names it knows (A, C, D for session-load), and pool named with only session-load arms is refused

gates.question: How is one rep's figure warm and how do the reps become a row?
options: one unmeasured replay of arm A first, then the median of the reps for each row, every arm and phase once per rep
no warm-up and the mean of the reps
gates.recommendation: one unmeasured replay of arm A first, then the median of the reps for each row, every arm and phase once per rep
gates.reason: the caches are warm for every measured rep, and one rep disturbed by other work on the host does not move the row
gates.answer: one unmeasured replay of arm A first, then the median of the reps for each row, every arm and phase once per rep

gates.question: How is the intake hook's start count pinned, since its drift scan runs item checks within a wall-clock budget and starts as many processes as fit?
options: one commit in the replay clone changes the mode of each item file, so no item is eligible and the scan runs no check; the real hook's cost with checks is not measured
changed-path filters in the clone's commit graph, so the scan is faster, but the checks it then runs still end at the budget
leave the clone as it is, the starts of both arms then move with the host's speed
gates.recommendation: one commit in the replay clone changes the mode of each item file, so no item is eligible and the scan runs no check; the real hook's cost with checks is not measured
gates.reason: measured over three replays of each arm, the filters left the intake hook between 950 and 974 starts and this leaves it at 944 in every replay, so A minus C is the hooks C leaves out by construction
gates.answer: one commit in the replay clone changes the mode of each item file, so no item is eligible and the scan runs no check; the real hook's cost with checks is not measured
